t.1.34.1: The Sūta said: Having heard the words of all of them, spoken thus and thus, and having heard the speech of Vāsuki, Elāpattra said this.
t.1.34.3: O king, whatever man here in this world is struck down by fate, he takes refuge in fate alone; there is no other final recourse in that case.
t.1.34.2: That sacrifice shall not take place, nor shall there be such a king, Janamejaya the descendant of Pāṇḍu, from whom great danger threatens us.
t.1.34.5: When the curse was pronounced, O best of serpents, I, having climbed onto my mother's lap out of fear, heard those words at that time.
t.1.34.4: This fear of ours, O best of serpents, is ordained by fate; in this matter we take refuge in fate alone, so listen to my words.
t.1.34.7: For what mother, O Grandsire, having obtained beloved sons, would curse them thus, except the fierce-natured Kadrū, O God of gods, in your very presence?
t.1.34.6: “The foremost of the serpents are cruel, cruel!” Such, O lord, was the cry of the gods, stricken with grief, when they approached the Grandfather, O greatly splendid one.
t.1.34.8: And you too, O Grandfather, said “So be it” to her word; we wish to know the reason why she was not restrained.
t.1.34.10: Those snakes that are biting, base, of wicked conduct and virulent with venom, they shall meet destruction, but not those who walk in the path of dharma.
t.1.34.9: Many are the serpents, fierce, of terrible might and virulent with venom; desiring the welfare of creatures, I did not restrain it then.
t.1.34.11: And learn from me the cause through which the release of those serpents from their great peril will come about, when that time has arrived in that manner.
t.1.34.12: In the family of the Yāyāvaras there will be a wise and great seer, renowned as Jaratkāru, full of splendor and with his senses under control.
t.1.34.13: To that Jaratkāru a son of great austerity will be born, Āstīka by name; he will then stop that sacrifice. There the serpents who are righteous will be set free.
t.1.34.14: O god, in whom will that foremost of sages, the mighty Jaratkāru of great austerities, beget a great-souled son?
t.1.34.15: O gods, that best of the twice-born, mighty and bearing the same name, will beget a mighty offspring upon a maiden who bears the same name as he.
t.1.34.16: Then the gods said to him, the Grandfather, "So be it!" And having spoken thus, the gods departed, and so did the god, the Grandfather.
t.1.34.17: Thus do I foresee it, O Vāsuki: your sister, who is known as Jaratkāru, give her to him in marriage.
t.1.34.18: To the seer of good vows who comes begging for her as one begs for alms, you must give her, so that the fear of the Nāgas may be allayed; this is the deliverance I have heard of.
